newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's ruling party moves against dissidents.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's ruling party moves against dissidents.

text.p: Mexico's ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) on Monday stepped up its attack on a rebellious faction of the party that threatened to disrupt a major convention last weekend.

PRI President Santiago Onate told reporters the offices of Democracia 2000, a reformist wing of the party that has ruled Mexico for 67 years, were shut down as part of "administrative measures" taken by the party.
Though Onate has pledged to make the party more democratic, it does not take internal dissent lightly.

The offices were shut down just two days after Democracia 2000 head Ramiro de la Rosa was grabbed and thrown out of the PRI's 17th National Assembly for calling former President Carlos Salinas de Gortari a "thief and a murderer" responsible for the death in 1994 of PRI presidential candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio.

Hatred of Salinas, who is a member of the PRI, is shared by many within the party since the ex-president fled into voluntary exile shortly after leaving office in December 1994 amid Mexico's worst economic collapse in 50 years.
But at its assembly the party tried hard to sweep its controversies under the carpet, and it fell short of expelling Salinas from its ranks.
